rules_evaluated.evidence: chunk 4 "Stashing and switching between sessions": line 68: "Agent committed to the wrong branch in one session? Don't tie your brain in knots. `git reset --soft HEAD~1` keeps the changes staged, switch branches, re-commit on the right one." — a wrong-branch git-reset recovery tip that isn't stashing or switching between sessions; the header doesn't literally summarize this closing beat of the chunk.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Give the wrong-branch fix its own short aside, or widen the header to cover session/branch recovery generally.

rules_evaluated.evidence: chunk 6 "When NOT to run multi-session": line 86: "3. **You are new to the loop.** If you are still learning what \"good\" looks like in one session, adding a second session adds variables, not learning." — bolds a full subject+verb lead sentence (a clause, not a sub-span handle), unlike its two list siblings ("**Ordering dependencies.**", "**Greedy parallelism on a small task.**") which bold noun-phrase handles.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Recast to a noun-phrase handle matching the other two items, e.g. "**New to the loop.**"
